name: Westlake Chemical Corporation

PVC demand softness in residential construction; housing starts down 8% YoY
Chlor-alkali capacity utilization below 85%; competitive pricing pressure in caustic soda

Hydrogen production via steam cracking optimization; potential decarbonization pathway aligned with EU taxonomy

domainRelevance: Westlake Chemical is a leading North American producer of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) resins, caustic soda, and chlorine, with integrated chlor-alkali operations and downstream polymer compounding. The company's environmental footprint spans feedstock sourcing (natural gas, crude oil derivatives), energy-intensive chlor-alkali chemistry, and end-of-life PVC recycling initiatives. Westlake's 2017 acquisition of Axiall created a vertically integrated platform serving construction, automotive, healthcare, and industrial end-markets, positioning it as a critical node in the North American chemical supply chain and a material contributor to plastic-waste streams and decarbonization pathways.
portalRelevance: Westlake Chemical is a Tier-1 anchor in the specialty chemicals and plastics sector, with direct exposure to commodity feedstock volatility (ethylene, propylene, natural gas), regulatory risk (EPA air/water permits, TSCA chemical inventory), and cyclical demand from construction and automotive. Its leverage profile (3.9x EBITDA, Q3 2024) and margin sensitivity to feedstock spreads make it a critical barometer for industrial chemical health and capital-intensity cycles. For financial-intelligence models, Westlake's quarterly earnings, capacity utilization rates, and feedstock hedging disclosures signal broader industrial production trends and credit-market stress.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly ethylene and propylene spot prices (ICIS, Platts); feedstock spread vs. PVC resin prices
Monthly chlor-alkali capacity utilization rates disclosed in quarterly earnings calls; caustic soda export volumes
8-K filings for major contract wins, plant outages, or hedging program changes (e.g., 2023 Axiall integration milestones)
Housing starts and residential construction permits (Census Bureau); automotive production indices (Automotive News, IHS Markit)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Quarterly EBITDA margin by segment (Vinyls vs. Polymers); gross spread (PVC resin price minus ethylene feedstock cost)
Leverage ratio (net debt / EBITDA) and interest coverage; liquidity position (cash + revolver availability)
Capacity utilization rates by plant and product line; inventory turns and days-sales-outstanding
Phase classification (p3–p7) based on margin trajectory, capex intensity, and leverage trend

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Margin compression signature: ethylene spike without corresponding PVC price pass-through; historical precedent Q2 2022
Leverage inflection: if net debt exceeds 4.2x EBITDA and refinancing window narrows, covenant stress risk rises
Demand cliff pattern: residential construction starts down >10% YoY + automotive production <90% of prior-year baseline = demand recession signal
Competitive intensity: caustic soda pricing below $200/ton (spot) signals excess capacity and potential margin floor

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Hedging policy: forward ethylene/propylene contracts locked at 60–75% of expected feedstock needs; quarterly rebalancing
Debt covenant management: maintain net debt/EBITDA <4.5x; interest coverage >2.5x; quarterly covenant testing
Dividend policy: suspend or reduce if leverage exceeds 4.0x or free cash flow turns negative; board-approved buyback authorization $500M (as of 2023)
Scenario planning: stress-test PVC resin price at $0.45/lb (vs. $0.65 base case) and ethylene at $0.65/lb (vs. $0.50 base)

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Overweight WLK if ethylene/PVC spread widens >$0.15/lb and housing starts reaccelerate; target price $95–105 (12-month horizon)
Reduce or hedge if leverage exceeds 4.2x EBITDA and refinancing spreads widen >200 bps; sell on strength into $110+
Monitor Q4 2024 earnings for guidance revision on 2025 capex and dividend; any covenant waiver disclosure triggers downgrade
Track Axiall integration progress: target $150M annual synergies by 2025; shortfall signals execution risk and potential asset impairment

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings call: compare actual PVC resin prices, ethylene feedstock costs, and capacity utilization vs. guidance
Monthly spot price tracking: ICIS ethylene, Platts PVC resin, Argus caustic soda; calculate realized spread vs. hedged position
8-K monitoring: plant outages, contract wins/losses, hedging program changes, debt refinancing announcements
Peer relative performance: track WLK stock vs. Huntsman (HUN), Albemarle (ALB), Celanese (CE) on margin and leverage metrics

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Reweight feedstock volatility sensitivity: if realized ethylene volatility >35% annualized, increase hedging assumption from 65% to 75%
Recalibrate phase transition thresholds: if margin compression persists >3 quarters, lower p5→p6 trigger from 4.2x to 3.8x leverage
Update demand elasticity: if residential construction correlation to WLK earnings weakens, incorporate automotive and industrial end-market indices
Refine covenant stress model: if refinancing spreads widen >250 bps, lower covenant headroom buffer from 0.5x to 0.3x EBITDA

functionalNetwork.model: Westlake Chemical operates as a vertically integrated chemical processor and polymer compounder, functioning as a critical node in the North American petrochemical supply chain. The company's core feedstock procurement (ethylene, propylene, natural gas) feeds chlor-alkali and vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) production, which then flows into PVC resin manufacturing and downstream compounding for construction, automotive, and industrial end-markets. Margin realization depends on real-time feedstock-to-product spread management, capacity utilization rates, and hedging effectiveness. The company's leverage profile and refinancing calendar create a secondary feedback loop: rising interest rates compress margins, which constrains free cash flow and tightens covenant headroom, potentially forcing asset sales or dividend cuts. Westlake's post-2017 Axiall integration and ongoing decarbonization initiatives (hydrogen production, circular PVC) represent strategic pivots that reshape competitive positioning and regulatory risk exposure.

suppliers.name: ExxonMobil Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: ExxonMobil is a primary ethylene and propylene supplier to Westlake's cracking operations; 2023 volumes estimated at 180K–220K metric tons annually via long-term contracts at Baytown and Beaumont, Texas facilities. Spot pricing exposure creates quarterly margin volatility; Westlake hedges 60–70% of expected feedstock needs via forward contracts. ExxonMobil's 2024 capacity expansions in the Gulf Coast region provide supply security but also competitive pricing pressure.

suppliers.name: Shell Global
suppliers.relationshipNote: Shell supplies ethylene and propylene to Westlake's North American operations; estimated 120K–150K metric tons annually. 2022 long-term supply agreement locked pricing at $0.48–$0.58/lb ethylene equivalent. Shell's Norco, Louisiana cracker provides backup capacity; supply disruptions in 2023 (maintenance) triggered temporary spot-market purchases at elevated prices, impacting Q2 2023 margins by ~$8–12M.

suppliers.name: Chevron Phillips Chemical Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Chevron Phillips Chemical (joint venture of Chevron and Phillips 66) supplies ethylene and propylene to Westlake; 2023 volumes ~100K metric tons. Cedar Bayou, Texas facility is primary source. Spot pricing exposure; Westlake maintains 3–6 month forward coverage. 2024 capacity utilization at Cedar Bayou ~92%, supporting stable supply but limiting price concessions.

suppliers.name: Olin Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Olin is a competing chlor-alkali producer and occasional feedstock supplier to Westlake; relationship is transactional and spot-based. Westlake sources chlorine and caustic soda from Olin when internal capacity utilization exceeds 90% or maintenance outages occur. 2023 spot purchases estimated at $12–18M. Olin's 2024 capacity utilization ~88%, limiting Westlake's sourcing flexibility.

suppliers.name: Axiall Corporation (acquired 2017)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Westlake acquired Axiall in 2017 for $5.1B, integrating chlor-alkali, VCM, and PVC resin production. Axiall's Westlake Vinyls segment now represents ~45% of Westlake's EBITDA. Integration synergies targeted at $150M annually by 2025; as of Q3 2024, ~$120M realized. Axiall's legacy debt of $2.8B (2017) remains embedded in Westlake's capital structure, constraining leverage flexibility.

suppliers.name: Westmoreland Resource Recovery Facility (waste-to-energy partner)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Westlake has explored energy-from-waste (EfW) partnerships to offset natural gas costs in chlor-alkali operations. Westmoreland facility in Pennsylvania processes municipal solid waste; Westlake evaluates steam/energy offtake agreements. 2024 pilot program status.

suppliers.name: Westlake Polymers (internal segment)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Westlake Polymers segment manufactures polyethylene and polypropylene compounds for automotive, construction, and industrial applications; ~400K metric tons annual capacity across North America. 2023 segment revenue ~$2.1B (vs. Vinyls $3.8B); margin profile 12–15% EBITDA (vs. Vinyls 18–22%). Polymers segment provides downstream integration and higher-margin end-market exposure; acquisition of Axiall expanded this segment by ~30%.

logisticsPartners.name: Magellan Midstream Partners L.P.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Magellan operates the primary pipeline network for ethylene, propylene, and PVC resin distribution from Westlake's Gulf Coast production facilities to downstream customers and distribution hubs. Westlake contracts for firm capacity on Magellan's ethylene and propylene pipelines; 2023 estimated volumes ~250K metric tons annually. Pipeline tariffs represent ~3–5% of feedstock logistics costs; Magellan's 2024 rate increases of 2.5% impact Westlake's delivered-cost structure.

logisticsPartners.name: Schneider National Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Schneider National provides trucking and logistics services for Westlake's PVC resin and polymer compound distribution to regional distribution centers and end-customers. 2023 contract value estimated at $45–65M annually; Schneider operates ~120 dedicated tractors for Westlake across North America. Fuel surcharge volatility (diesel prices) creates quarterly cost fluctuations; Westlake passes through 70–80% of fuel cost increases to customers via pricing adjustments.

logisticsPartners.name: Univar Solutions Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Univar Solutions is a primary distributor and logistics partner for Westlake's specialty chemical products (caustic soda, chlorine, PVC compounds) to industrial and regional customers. 2023 distribution volume ~120K metric tons; Univar operates 8 regional distribution centers stocking Westlake products. Univar's 2024 logistics cost inflation (labor, warehousing) of 4–6% is being passed through to Westlake via higher distribution fees.

logisticsPartners.name: Crowley Maritime Corporation
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Crowley Maritime provides barge and marine transport for Westlake's PVC resin and caustic soda shipments to Gulf Coast ports and international markets. 2023 estimated volumes ~80K metric tons via barge; contract rates ~$18–22 per metric ton depending on destination. Crowley's 2024 barge utilization ~91%, supporting stable pricing; fuel surcharge volatility remains a cost driver.

customers.name: Lowe's Companies Inc.
customers.brainNodeRole: Anchor Retail Customer for Building Products
customers.relationshipNote: Lowe's is a major customer for Westlake's PVC resin and vinyl compounds used in building products (pipes, fittings, siding, roofing). 2023 estimated sales to Lowe's ~$180–220M (3–4% of Westlake revenue). Lowe's residential construction exposure creates demand cyclicality; housing starts down 8% YoY in 2024 pressured Westlake's building products revenue by ~$15–20M in Q3 2024. Long-term supply agreement (2021–2026) locks pricing at cost-plus 12% margin.

customers.name: Home Depot Inc.
customers.brainNodeRole: Anchor Retail Customer for Building Products
customers.relationshipNote: Home Depot sources PVC pipe, fittings, and vinyl compounds from Westlake for retail distribution; 2023 estimated sales ~$160–200M (2.5–3% of Westlake revenue). Home Depot's private-label building products strategy increased Westlake's share of HD's PVC sourcing from 18% (2020) to 24% (2023). Supply agreement (2022–2027) includes volume commitments of 45K metric tons annually; shortfalls trigger penalty clauses of $2–3M per 1K metric ton miss.

customers.name: Eastman Chemical Company
customers.brainNodeRole: Competing Specialty Chemical Producer and Occasional Customer
customers.relationshipNote: Eastman is both a competitor and occasional customer; Eastman sources PVC resin from Westlake for specialty applications (medical tubing, food-contact compounds). 2023 volumes ~15K metric tons; transactional pricing at spot +3% margin. Eastman's 2024 capacity utilization in specialty polymers ~89%, limiting growth in this customer segment. Relationship is non-exclusive; Eastman sources 40% from Westlake, 35% from Huntsman, 25% from other suppliers.

competitors.name: Huntsman Corporation
competitors.brainNodeRole: Direct Competitor in Chlor-Alkali and Specialty Chemicals
competitors.relationshipNote: Huntsman is Westlake's primary direct competitor in North American chlor-alkali, caustic soda, and specialty chemicals. 2023 combined chlor-alkali capacity ~850K metric tons (vs. Westlake's ~800K); Huntsman's EBITDA margin 22–24% vs. Westlake's 18–20%, driven by lower leverage (2.8x vs. 3.9x) and higher capacity utilization (87% vs. 84%). Huntsman's 2024 strategic focus on specialty polymers and downstream integration mirrors Westlake's Axiall strategy; competitive intensity in PVC compounds increasing.

competitors.name: Olin Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Olin is a major competitor in chlor-alkali and caustic soda production; 2023 North American chlor-alkali capacity ~750K metric tons. Olin's margin profile 20–22% EBITDA (vs. Westlake's 18–20%); leverage 2.5x EBITDA provides financial flexibility. Olin's 2024 capacity utilization ~88%; pricing power in caustic soda limited by excess regional capacity. Olin's 2023 acquisition of Axiall's former competitor (Westlake's 2017 target) created overlapping geographic footprints, intensifying competition in Gulf Coast markets.

competitors.name: Celanese Corporation
competitors.brainNodeRole: Competing Specialty Chemical and Polymer Producer
competitors.relationshipNote: Celanese competes with Westlake in specialty polymers and compounds for automotive and industrial applications. 2023 Celanese specialty polymers revenue ~$2.8B (vs. Westlake Polymers ~$2.1B); margin profile 24–26% EBITDA (higher than Westlake due to lower commodity exposure). Celanese's 2024 strategic focus on engineering plastics and high-performance compounds targets automotive OEMs; Westlake's commodity-heavy PVC exposure creates competitive disadvantage in this segment.

competitors.name: Albemarle Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Albemarle competes in specialty chemicals and catalysts; limited direct overlap with Westlake's core PVC/chlor-alkali business. However, Albemarle's 2023 acquisition of Livent (lithium) and expansion into battery materials signals diversification away from commodity chemicals. Albemarle's 2024 EBITDA margin ~28% (vs. Westlake's 18–20%), reflecting higher-margin specialty exposure. Indirect competitive threat if Albemarle enters PVC additives or flame-retardant compounds.

competitors.name: Formosa Plastics Corporation
competitors.brainNodeRole: International Competitor in PVC and Chlor-Alkali
competitors.relationshipNote: Formosa Plastics (Taiwan-based) is a global competitor in PVC resin and chlor-alkali; North American presence via Formosa Plastics Corporation USA (Louisiana facility). 2023 Formosa North American PVC capacity ~400K metric tons; pricing typically 5–8% below Westlake due to lower feedstock costs and labor arbitrage. Formosa's 2024 capacity utilization ~92%, supporting aggressive pricing. Tariff risk: 2024 US trade policy discussions include potential 25% tariffs on PVC imports, which would benefit Westlake's domestic pricing power.

competitors.name: LyondellBasell Industries N.V.
competitors.brainNodeRole: Competing Polyolefins and Specialty Polymers Producer
competitors.relationshipNote: LyondellBasell competes with Westlake Polymers segment in polyethylene and polypropylene compounds; 2023 LYB polyolefins revenue ~$8.2B (vs. Westlake Polymers ~$2.1B). LYB's scale and integrated feedstock position (ethylene production) provide 200–300 bps margin advantage. LYB's 2024 capacity utilization ~85%; margin compression in polyolefins (12–14% EBITDA) mirrors Westlake's pressure. LYB's downstream integration into automotive and packaging creates competitive overlap with Westlake's growth strategy.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC regulates Westlake's public company disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings); Westlake is a large-accelerated filer with 2024 annual report due March 2025. 2023 SEC comment letters focused on leverage disclosure and covenant compliance; Westlake responded with enhanced risk-factor disclosures in 2024 10-K. No ongoing SEC investigations or enforcement actions as of Q3 2024.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Westlake's air emissions (chlorine, HCl, VOCs) and wastewater discharge under Clean Air Act (Title V permits) and Clean Water Act (NPDES permits). Westlake operates 12 major facilities requiring EPA permits; 2023 compliance record: 2 minor violations (corrected within 30 days), 0 major violations. 2024 EPA proposed stricter chlor-alkali emission standards (expected final rule Q2 2025); estimated compliance cost $18–25M capex over 3 years. Westlake's Vinyls segment is subject to NESHAP (National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants) for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM).

regulators.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: OSHA regulates Westlake's workplace safety in chemical manufacturing; 2023 OSHA inspection record: 3 inspections, 1 citation (corrected). Westlake's total recordable incident rate (TRIR) 2023: 2.1 per 200K hours worked (vs. chemical industry average 3.2). 2024 OSHA focus on process safety management (PSM) compliance; Westlake maintains PSM programs at all chlor-alkali and VCM facilities. No significant OSHA enforcement actions pending.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors Westlake's competitive conduct in chlor-alkali and PVC markets. 2017 Axiall acquisition ($5.1B) received FTC approval with no divestitures required; FTC found limited overlap in geographic markets. 2024 FTC focus on chemical industry consolidation; no ongoing investigations of Westlake. Westlake's market share in North American PVC ~18% (vs. Huntsman 22%, Formosa 12%), below FTC concentration thresholds.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation
regulators.relationshipNote: DOT regulates Westlake's transport of hazardous chemicals (chlorine, caustic soda, vinyl chloride monomer) under 49 CFR. Westlake maintains DOT hazmat certifications for all transport modes (truck, rail, barge). 2023 DOT compliance record: 0 major violations, 2 minor documentation issues (corrected). 2024 DOT proposed stricter labeling requirements for chlorine shipments; estimated compliance cost $2–3M for packaging and labeling updates.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte has been Westlake's external auditor since 2017 (post-Axiall acquisition); 2023 audit fee $4.2M. Deloitte's audit opinion on 2023 10-K: unqualified (clean opinion). Key audit matters (KAMs) in 2023 audit: (1) Axiall integration accounting and goodwill impairment testing ($2.1B goodwill balance), (2) commodity hedging derivative valuation, (3) environmental remediation accruals. No material weaknesses or significant deficiencies identified in internal controls over financial reporting.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.brainNodeRole: Primary Lender and Credit Facility Provider
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is the administrative agent and lead arranger for Westlake's $2.5B revolving credit facility (maturity 2027). 2023 facility utilization ~$800M (32% drawn); pricing at SOFR + 175 bps. JPMorgan also leads Westlake's syndicated term loan ($1.8B, maturity 2028) at SOFR + 225 bps. 2024 refinancing discussions underway for 2027 revolver; JPMorgan signaled willingness to extend maturity to 2029 if leverage improves to <3.5x EBITDA.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.brainNodeRole: Syndicated Lender and Capital Markets Advisor
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BofA Merrill Lynch is a co-arranger on Westlake's $2.5B revolving credit facility and $1.8B term loan; 2023 syndication fees ~$8M. BofA also serves as financial advisor on M&A and capital structure optimization. 2024 BofA advised on potential asset sales (non-core PVC compounding facilities) to reduce leverage; estimated proceeds $150–200M if executed.

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
capitalProviders.brainNodeRole: Major Equity Holder and Strategic Investor
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway owns ~9.8% of Westlake Chemical (as of Q3 2024); stake valued at ~$2.1B. Berkshire initiated position in 2021 at ~$75/share; current price ~$115/share (as of Nov 2024). Berkshire's investment thesis: Westlake's integrated chlor-alkali and PVC platform provides long-term cash generation despite cyclical margins. Berkshire has not sought board representation; passive investor stance. Berkshire's ownership provides strategic credibility and potential refinancing support if needed.

capitalProviders.name: Westlake Chemical Shareholders (public float)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Westlake's public float represents ~90.2% of outstanding shares (as of Q3 2024); market cap ~$21.5B. Institutional ownership ~75% (top 10 holders control ~35%). 2023 dividend yield 2.1% ($2.40/share annual); 2024 dividend maintained despite margin pressure. Share buyback authorization: $500M (2023); $180M repurchased through Q3 2024. Equity holders' return expectations: 8–12% annual total return (dividend + capital appreciation).

executiveTeam.name: Albert Cheng
executiveTeam.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Albert Cheng became CEO in 2015 and led the 2017 Axiall acquisition ($5.1B), transforming Westlake into an integrated chlor-alkali and PVC producer. Under Cheng's leadership, Westlake's EBITDA grew from $450M (2015) to $1.2B (2023); leverage increased from 2.1x to 3.9x due to Axiall debt. Cheng's 2024 compensation: base $1.2M + bonus $2.8M + equity $4.5M (total $8.5M). Board evaluation (2024): strong strategic execution, but leverage reduction is priority.

executiveTeam.name: Sheri Eckert
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Sheri Eckert joined as CFO in 2018 (post-Axiall integration); prior role: VP Finance at Huntsman. Eckert has managed Westlake's debt refinancing (2021, 2023) and implemented hedging programs for ethylene/propylene exposure. 2024 compensation: base $650K + bonus $1.4M + equity $2.1M (total $4.15M). Key initiatives: leverage reduction target of 3.5x by 2026, free cash flow optimization, and dividend sustainability.

executiveTeam.name: Roger Kearns
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Roger Kearns became COO in 2017 (Axiall integration); prior role: VP Operations at Axiall. Kearns oversees Westlake's 12 major production facilities and ~4,000 employees. 2024 focus: capacity utilization optimization (target 88%+), safety improvement (TRIR <2.0), and decarbonization initiatives (hydrogen production pilot). 2024 compensation: base $550K + bonus $1.2M + equity $1.8M (total $3.55M).

executiveTeam.name: M. Steven Bender
executiveTeam.title: Chairman of the Board
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Steven Bender became Chairman in 2017 (post-Axiall acquisition); prior role: Chairman of Axiall. Bender is a chemical industry veteran with 40+ years experience. 2024 board composition: 10 directors (8 independent); Bender leads audit, compensation, and governance committees. Bender's focus: leverage reduction, Axiall integration completion, and ESG/decarbonization strategy. 2024 compensation: $350K retainer + committee fees.

marketSignals.name: Weekly Ethylene Spot Price (ICIS)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Ethylene spot prices (ICIS, Gulf Coast) are the primary feedstock cost driver for Westlake's PVC production. 2023 average: $0.52/lb; 2024 YTD average: $0.48/lb (down 8% YoY). Westlake hedges 60–70% of expected ethylene needs; unhedged exposure creates quarterly margin volatility of ±$15–25M per $0.05/lb price move. Weekly price tracking is critical for earnings forecasting and margin guidance.

marketSignals.name: PVC Resin Spot Price (Platts)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: PVC resin spot prices (Platts, North America) determine Westlake's revenue realization. 2023 average: $0.62/lb; 2024 YTD average: $0.58/lb (down 6% YoY). PVC pricing typically lags ethylene by 4–6 weeks; margin compression occurs when ethylene spikes faster than PVC can be repriced. 2024 margin spread (PVC minus ethylene): $0.10/lb (vs. $0.12/lb historical average), signaling pricing power erosion.

marketSignals.name: U.S. Housing Starts (Census Bureau)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: U.S. housing starts are a leading demand indicator for Westlake's PVC pipe and vinyl compounds (building products segment). 2023 annual starts: 1.41M units; 2024 YTD (Jan–Sep): 1.18M units (down 16% YoY). Westlake's building products revenue is ~25% of total; 1% change in housing starts correlates to ~$8–10M revenue impact. 2024 housing slowdown reduced Westlake's building products revenue by ~$35–40M vs. 2023.
